objects.title: MAAT
objects.summary: A museum on the Tagus bringing art, architecture and technology together in a riverside setting.
objects.why: The building, exhibitions, riverfront and Belém can be explored as one connected experience rather than as separate listings.

objects.title: Belém
objects.summary: A riverfront district where monuments, museums, gardens and food can be experienced within one walkable area.
objects.why: Belém works as a cluster of connected places rather than a checklist of isolated attractions.

objects.title: Calçada portuguesa
objects.summary: Lisbon’s black-and-white stone paving turns the ground itself into a piece of public design.
objects.why: The paving is a strong example of the Story layer: something people walk over every day becomes a way to understand craft, pattern and identity.

objects.title: Fado and the city
objects.summary: Fado connects voice, neighbourhood, memory and the rooms where the music is performed.
objects.why: Rather than treating fado as a venue category, LBNB can connect the music to the neighbourhoods and experiences that give it context.

objects.title: Lisbon through architecture
objects.summary: A self-guided architectural thread connecting riverfront buildings, streets and the stories behind them.
objects.why: It demonstrates how one Journey can connect several Places and Stories without requiring a commercial booking.

objects.title: Beirut
objects.summary: A city best entered through neighbourhoods, streets, food, architecture and the relationships between them.
objects.why: Beirut is exactly the kind of destination where the product should reveal multiple overlapping identities rather than flatten the city into a list of attractions.

objects.title: Jbeil / Byblos
objects.summary: A historic Mediterranean town where archaeology, old streets, the harbour and contemporary life overlap.
objects.why: Byblos can connect history to present-day experience in one compact destination graph.

objects.title: Baalbek
objects.summary: A major archaeological site in the Beqaa, centred on monumental Roman temple remains.
objects.why: Baalbek gives the Place layer enough depth to connect archaeology, landscape and historical Story without reducing the visit to a single photo stop.

objects.title: The Lebanese table
objects.summary: Food understood as a network of dishes, ingredients, rituals, regions and people rather than simply restaurant search.
objects.why: This Story can connect food Places and Experiences across Beirut, Jbeil and the mountains.

objects.title: From coast to the Beqaa
objects.summary: A conceptual Journey thread linking Jbeil / Byblos with Baalbek and the stories that sit between coast and inland Lebanon.
objects.why: It tests how the product can assemble a larger experience from several Places without pretending that the experience has to be a commercial tour.

reels.caption: Start with the building, then let the riverfront open the rest of Belém.
Sometimes the city is already telling its story under your feet.
Beirut is not one story. Start with the city, then follow the layers around it.
A historic town can be a Place, a Story and the beginning of a larger Journey.
Open the monument, then keep following what connects beyond it.
